title: Conversion between the numerical simulation and the calculation using the Deformation Energy Ratio approach
author: Golubiatnikov, Wald

steps.title: Define geometry and notch parameters
steps.instruction: Select plate width w and set notch depth ratio d/w between the minimum 0.06 (derived from NPlEN ≥ NUEN with γM0 = 1) and the maximum ≈0.2 (derived from bolted‑hole limit w = 2e₂ with edge distance e ≥ 1.2 d). Choose a notch radius that gives the desired stress‑concentration factor (SCF) of 2, 2.5, 3, or 4. Set the length of the free sections to 120 mm to avoid boundary‑condition effects.

steps.title: Build finite‑element model in ANSYS
steps.instruction: Create the model in ANSYS 2022 R2 using the real material properties [fyR, fUR, εUR] for the simulation and the nominal properties [fyEN, fUEN, εUEN] for the calculation. Mesh the geometry with 20‑node solid elements of size 2 mm × 2 mm.

steps.title: Run numerical simulation (real material)
steps.instruction: Perform a static analysis with the real‑material model. Record the complete stress‑strain curve and compute the total deformation energy EUR as the area under this curve. Identify the point (fUR, εUR) where necking begins.

steps.title: Run numerical calculation (nominal material)
steps.instruction: Repeat the static analysis using the nominal‑material model. Obtain its stress‑strain curve and calculate the total deformation energy EUEN (area under the curve). Identify the point (fUEN, εUEN).

steps.title: Determine design ultimate resistance from simulation
steps.instruction: Calculate the design ultimate resistance NUR from the simulation results using Eq. (2). Locate the stress σNuR and strain εNuR at NUR (example: σNuR = 344.01 MPa, εNuR = 0.4 %). Compute the deformation energy ENuR as the area under the simulation curve up to (σNuR, εNuR); in the example ENuR/EUR = 4.35 % (ENuR = 0.0435 × 24.77).

steps.title: Compute deformation energy for calculation
steps.instruction: Apply the deformation‑energy‑ratio equality ENuR/EUR = ENuEN/EUEN and solve for ENuEN: ENuEN = (ENuR × EUEN) / EUR. Using the example values ENuR = 1.075, EUEN = 27.69, EUR = 24.77 gives ENuEN ≈ 1.205.

steps.title: Iteratively find limiting stress and strain for calculation
steps.instruction: Adjust σNuEN and εNuEN on the nominal‑material stress‑strain curve until the area under the curve up to (σNuEN, εNuEN) equals ENuEN. Record the converged values (example: σNuEN = 289.6 MPa, εNuEN = 0.43 %).

steps.title: Calculate design ultimate resistance for calculation
steps.instruction: Compute the design ultimate resistance for the calculation as NUEN = σNuEN × Anet / γM0 (γM0 = 1). In the example NUEN ≈ 70.43 kN, which matches the recommended value of 70.04 kN.

steps.title: Validate results against analytical values
steps.instruction: Compare NUEN with the analytical resistance obtained from Eq. (2). Ensure the deviation is within acceptable limits (maximum observed 5.6 % for the smallest notch, average deviation < 5 %). Repeat the procedure for all samples (40 in the study) if required.
